source_excerpts.text:
I constructed a different reusable mechanism: **a reliable logical measurement driven by an unknown, positive operator-valued force**. The medium can remain uninitialized, strongly interacting, and correlated with the data and a reference. Its internal motion can change the magnitude of the force without spoiling the measurement.

The central result is an instrument theorem, not just an outcome-probability identity. That distinction lets the measurements compose into useful quantum dynamics. I verified an exact CNOT construction with an initially dirty ancillary qubit, and checked the corresponding \(H\), \(S\), and \(T\) teleportation identities.

This changes the native interface. It requires a qualified joint-parity force, a meter source and readout, and classical adaptation. It does **not** establish that those resources are cheaper to build than a conventional parity meter. What it establishes is that, for this interface, fine gain estimation and a nearly frozen medium are unnecessary.

The earlier five-scalar gate, inverse-chirality obstruction, scalar-effect identities, forward-bath bounds, and failures remain intact. The new work retains **root-working status**.

## 1. Why I changed the primitive

I treated robust phase estimation as a serious competitor. The corrected Kimmel–Low–Yoder analysis retains Heisenberg scaling, but its phase-unwrapping guarantee uses the stricter \(\pi/(3k)\) condition; the original \(\pi/(2k)\) analysis did not establish the claimed failure bound. Its useful resource remains long coherent interrogation. The earlier scalar measurement effects do not, by themselves, supply that resource in a moving bath. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="0"}

I also examined protection throughout the control path. Dynamically corrected gates have substantive control and error-strength hypotheses. Noiseless-subsystem control provides another route: sufficiently symmetric bath motion can be strong while exchange operations remain protected. Those are useful ordinary methods, but their qualification requirements matter. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="1"}

That route clarified the remaining problem. Even if symmetry makes a long gain probe legal, the probe still spends time resolving a phase. A logical measurement has a different requirement: its eigenspaces must lead to distinguishable records, while coherence inside each eigenspace survive
